Your impact begins here

Shape how AI transforms manufacturing and corporate functions by turning strategic ambition into clear, actionable demand that delivers real value.

As AI Demand & Portfolio Manager, you will be the primary Enterprise AI demand-management partner for Global Manufacturing & Supply (GMS) and Corporate Functions, including Quality. You will bridge business priorities and AI delivery, ensuring demand is proactively identified, clearly articulated and aligned to create measurable impact.

What you’ll bring

To succeed in this role, you will bring:

• 7+ years of relevant experience in demand management, portfolio or product management, digital or AI transformation, strategy, business partnering or management consulting in a complex global organisation

• Demonstrated ability to shape ambiguous business needs into clear, outcome-oriented initiatives and mobilise cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders without direct authority

• Practical understanding of the AI, data or digital product lifecycle, including discovery, feasibility, data readiness, responsible AI and risk considerations, delivery, adoption and value measurement

• Proven experience developing value cases, benefits-tracking approaches, KPIs and executive-level portfolio or demand reporting

• A relevant Master’s degree in business, engineering, technology, data, economics or a related field, or equivalent professional experience

• Fluent written and spoken English

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience working with manufacturing and supply-chain environments and/or Corporate Functions. Exposure to both is an advantage

• Experience in life sciences, pharmaceuticals or another regulated industry

What you’ll do

In this role, you will:

• Build proactive engagement with leaders across GMS and Corporate Functions, in collaboration with Enterprise AI Delivery Teams, to identify strategic priorities, operational pain points and emerging AI opportunities while maintaining a complete and transparent view of demand

• Lead discovery and intake sessions that translate ambiguous business needs into concise problem statements and outcome hypotheses, with clear ownership, value definition, success measures, dependencies and readiness criteria

• Orchestrate end-to-end demand alignment by connecting related requests, identifying duplication and reuse opportunities, and routing demand to the right Enterprise AI teams and governance forums

• Convene and influence stakeholders across AI delivery, data, architecture, security, privacy, legal, risk and compliance to drive action, resolve ambiguity and surface trade-offs

• Define value hypotheses, baselines, indicators and follow-up cadences with business owners and AI delivery teams, maintaining visibility of value commitments and challenging gaps

• Provide management and governance with clear demand and value insights, including pipeline coverage, maturity, cycle time, bottlenecks and portfolio balance

• Promote a problem-first, value-led approach to AI demand while encouraging reuse, scalability and cross-domain synergies

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Enterprise AI function within Enterprise IT & Quality, where a growing team is shaping how AI capabilities are identified, governed and scaled across Novo Nordisk.

Working at the intersection of business strategy, AI delivery and portfolio governance, you will collaborate with leaders across GMS and Corporate Functions, Enterprise AI Delivery Teams and colleagues across data, architecture, security, privacy, legal, risk and compliance.

Together, you will connect ambition with execution across some of our most complex domains.

What you can expect here

In Enterprise IT & Quality, you will be part of an area that drives impact across the full Novo Nordisk value chain. We stay close to our stakeholders in the business to understand their needs and help reach millions of people living with serious chronic diseases.

Our focus is on ensuring the highest quality for patients, being a trusted technology leader and operating as an environmentally responsible business.

At Novo Nordisk, you’ll join a global healthcare company with opportunities for continuous learning and career development, alongside benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Every day, we seek solutions that defeat serious chronic diseases. For more than 100 years, curiosity, determination and a commitment to finding better ways forward have shaped how we work. Here, diverse thinking, shared purpose and mutual respect come together to create lasting change.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 742,600.00 to 1,091,600.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

Placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience.

Incentives and benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

If you’re ready to turn complex business needs into AI opportunities with measurable value, we’d like to hear from you.

Apply by 29 November 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis.

As IT and automation engineer, you will keep the equipment behind our medicines running reliably. Working hands-on with PLCs, SCADA/HMI systems and industrial networks, you will troubleshoot TFF systems, lyophilisers, chromatography skids and clean utilities across our development pilot plants and production facilities. Your work keeps this equipment available, compliant and secure, so medicines for clinical trials and worldwide market supply keep moving for people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

Our scope is broad, spanning server infrastructure, automation interfaces, compliance and project delivery. No one is an expert in all of it, and you don’t need to be. A solid foundation in IT/OT infrastructure, a proactive problem-solving mindset and the curiosity to grow into the rest matter as much as ticking every box.

• A technical background in automation, electrical engineering, industrial technology, IT/OT or similar, through education or practical experience.

• Hands-on experience with PLC, SCADA/HMI or automated industrial equipment.

• A good understanding of industrial automation, instrumentation and communication between equipment and control systems.

• Strong practical troubleshooting skills and curiosity about how equipment works.

• The ability to work independently on technical tasks while collaborating with different technical disciplines.

• Good communication skills and fluency in English.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience with Siemens PLCs, TIA Portal or similar automation platforms.

• Experience with OPC UA, industrial Ethernet or industrial networking.

• Experience with Industrial PCs, Windows-based automation systems or servers.

• Experience from a pharmaceutical, biotech or other regulated production environment.

• Knowledge of GxP, IT/OT system validation or cybersecurity.

What you’ll do

You will work close to the equipment, finding the cause of problems quickly and helping keep systems reliable and operational throughout their lifecycle.

• Troubleshoot PLC-based automation, I/O, instrumentation and equipment interfaces, and support, configure and troubleshoot SCADA/HMI systems.

• Resolve communication issues between PLCs, SCADA/HMI, servers and equipment, using technologies such as OPC UA and industrial Ethernet.

• Investigate equipment failures and identify root causes across automation, hardware, software and communication.

• Support patching, software upgrades, hardware replacement and lifecycle activities, as well as the day-to-day compliance and IT security of the automation and IT/OT components.

• Provide hands-on technical support during installation, commissioning, testing and handover of new or upgraded equipment.

• Maintain technical documentation, support change control and validation activities, and take part in the rotating on-call scheme for critical manufacturing equipment.

Who you’ll work with

You will join CMC IT Operations & Digitalisation, part of Chemistry, Manufacturing & Control (CMC) in Global Manufacturing & Supply. In CMC, we translate research into medicines for clinical trials and market supply worldwide. Our team provides the reliable, compliant and secure IT/OT foundation for the equipment across our development pilot plants and production facilities.

Day to day, you will work closely with equipment owners, IT/OT experts and vendors on support, maintenance, upgrades and new equipment. Bringing these perspectives together helps you get to the root of a problem faster and keep production moving. You will report to Asger Cederberg.

What you can expect here

You will work with a wide range of equipment and technologies, from automation and industrial networks to servers and validation, and you will be encouraged to build new skills across them. We value practical engineering curiosity and a willingness to learn, so you will be supported to grow into the areas that are new to you while contributing your own expertise from day one.

You will be trusted to work independently, make your voice heard and take ownership of technical problems, alongside colleagues who share knowledge and help each other perform at their best.

As IT Operation & Compliance Specialist, you will take technical ownership of the IT/OT equipment and automation platforms that keep our pilot plants and production facilities running reliably. You will set direction on connectivity, integration and validation, and right-size every technical set-up so it is compliant, secure and no more complex than it needs to be. Your decisions help turn research into medicines for clinical trials and market supply, for people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

You are a technical expert who is comfortable bridging IT, automation and validation, and who can make clear decisions on complex topics.

• A relevant Master’s degree in Engineering, Automation, Computer Science, IT or a similar technical field.

• Solid experience with IT/OT equipment, automation or validation in a regulated environment.

• A good understanding of GxP, IT/OT system validation and risk-based validation.

• A strong understanding of integration between PLCs, SCADA/HMI, servers, networks and PCS.

• The ability to handle complex technical topics independently and provide technical direction.

• Strong collaboration skills and fluency in English.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience with GAMP 5, IEC 62443, EU Cyber Resilience Act, data integrity, EU Annex 11 or 21 CFR Part 11.

• Experience with OPC UA, industrial Ethernet, PLC/SCADA communication and industrial networking.

• Experience validating interfaces and data flows between manufacturing equipment and surrounding systems.

• Experience with IT/OT cybersecurity, firewall zoning or network segmentation.

What you’ll do

You will be the go-to expert for IT/OT equipment across our production facilities, from early project phases through the full equipment lifecycle.

• Set technical direction and drive decisions across IT, automation and validation, challenging proposed designs and resolving complex cross-disciplinary issues.

• Define how equipment, PLCs, SCADA/HMI, servers and surrounding systems connect, so data flows are reliable, secure and validated.

• Own the risk-based validation approach for IT/OT equipment, so systems are fit for intended use and stay compliant throughout their lifecycle.

• Lead IT/OT and validation workstreams in equipment and facility projects, shaping architecture, requirements and technical design.

• Provide technical direction on IT/OT cybersecurity, including risk assessments, secure connectivity, network segmentation and vulnerability management.

• Assess upgrades, patches, changes and End-of-Life replacements from a technical, validation and operational perspective.

• Shape technical standards, validation approaches and ways of working across IT/OT, and take part in the rotating on-call scheme for critical manufacturing infrastructure.

Who you’ll work with

You will join CMC IT Operations & Digitalisation within Chemistry, Manufacturing & Control (CMC), part of Global Manufacturing & Supply. CMC translates research into medicines for clinical trials and market supply worldwide, and our team provides the reliable, compliant and secure IT/OT foundation that our pilot plants and production facilities depend on.

Day to day, you will work closely with automation engineers, equipment owners, Quality, validation specialists and project teams, as well as equipment suppliers. You will also provide specialist expertise to international projects and collaborate with our sister sites in the Czech Republic and the US.

You will bring different perspectives together, create clarity on priorities and help colleagues move quickly from technical question to decision. Reporting line: Asger Cederberg.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take ownership, make your voice heard and influence decisions that reach well beyond individual systems and projects. The role gives you room to grow your expertise across IT, automation and validation, and to build new skills through international collaboration with colleagues in different sites and functions.

Please note the practical side of the role: you can expect around 10–20 days of travel per year, and you will take part in a rotating on-call scheme for critical manufacturing infrastructure.

Help turn business priorities into organisational change that works in practice. As Organisational Development Partner, you will own defined OD projects and workstreams, diagnose what needs to change and give leaders clear options and recommendations. Working across functions and Executive Vice President (EVP) areas, you will help build the capabilities, accountabilities and ways of working that enable teams to deliver for people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

• A relevant master’s degree in business, strategy, organisation, HR or a related field.

• Typically, 4+ years of relevant experience in organisational development or design, consulting, or strategic HR with substantial OD delivery.

• Experience diagnosing organisational challenges, developing design options and supporting implementation.

• A track record of owning projects or workstreams and engaging senior stakeholders in an international environment.

• Strong analytical and facilitation skills, with practical experience using OD methods and workforce insights to develop clear recommendations.

• The initiative to take ownership, follow through on agreed actions and seek input from colleagues when it adds value.

• Clear communication and the confidence to challenge constructively, navigate competing priorities and balance analysis with practical delivery.

• Hands-on experience applying generative AI to organisational development, including prompt engineering, preparing data and context for AI analysis, and checking outputs for accuracy and bias when analysing workforce data or testing organisation design options.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience in change management and/or mergers and acquisitions (M&A) from a people and capability perspective.

What you’ll do

You will deliver agreed outcomes within a clear mandate, drawing on the expertise of your manager and colleagues while taking ownership of your assignments.

• Frame organisational challenges with business leaders, HR Business Partners and strategy colleagues. Agree the problem to solve, scope and intended outcomes.

• Develop organisation and operating model options that connect strategy and capabilities with structures, processes, people and measures of performance. Explain the trade-offs and recommend a direction.

• Combine workforce and organisational data with business insight to prepare concise recommendations and decision materials, partnering with People Analytics on analytical needs.

• Plan and deliver agreed projects or workstreams. Manage milestones and dependencies, track progress and raise issues together with proposed solutions.

• Agree implementation ownership with business leaders and HR Business Partners, and follow up on actions, adoption and results.

• Facilitate working sessions, share practical tools and guidance with leaders and HR Business Partners, and improve OD methods by sharing lessons from delivery.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Organisational Development and M&A team in People, Organisation & Corporate Affairs (POCA), reporting directly to the Head of Organisational Development and M&A.

Your partners will include business leaders, Corporate Strategy, strategy colleagues across EVP areas, HR Business Partners, People Analytics, Centres of Excellence and executive offices/EAs.

Based at headquarters in Denmark, you will work across functions, EVP areas and geographies, with guidance from your manager and colleagues on complex issues.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to own your assignments and make your voice heard, with clear expectations and support from experienced OD colleagues. The role offers exposure across the Novo value chain and the opportunity to deepen your OD skills through practical delivery.

We value thoughtful challenge, shared ownership and high-quality delivery. We learn from each other, follow through on decisions and approach change with care for people and integrity.

What we offer

At Novo, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage. This is a 12-month temporary position, with the potential to transition into a permanent role within the team.

As Senior Environmental Monitoring Process Scientist, you will bring your expertise to the M1 team in Kalundborg and help keep classified production areas in a controlled state. You will support colleagues through excursions and deviations and turn technical knowledge into practical advice. Your work helps keep API production running to the quality standards that people living with serious chronic diseases rely on.

What you’ll bring

You know what it takes to keep a classified production area in control, and you can explain it clearly to people with different professional backgrounds.

You bring:

• An academic degree in microbiology or a similar field.

• 5+ years of Environmental Monitoring experience from pharmaceutical production.

• Hands-on experience from classified production areas.

• Solid knowledge of GMP and the requirements for classified environments.

• Professional English and a willingness to learn Danish.

On a personal level you are a strong collaborator and communicator. You work easily with colleagues across teams, get your message across clearly, and are confident having difficult conversations and giving constructive feedback. You plan and prioritise independently and bring a pragmatic mindset that helps shape the direction of the work and focuses on what matters most.

What you’ll do

As our new Senior Environmental Monitoring Process Scientist, you will play a key role in strengthening and developing Environmental Monitoring (EM) in M1. You will work close to production and collaborate across functions to ensure robust EM processes and a strong state of compliance. As a senior member of the team, you will take ownership of complex challenges and drive improvements from idea to implementation.

Your tasks will include:

• Taking the lead on complex EM challenges and driving systematic problem-solving

• Analysing EM data and trends and translating insights into relevant actions and improvements

• Driving process improvements and optimisation in close collaboration with production and other stakeholders

• Supporting production in daily operations, including deviations, investigations, corrective actions and change requests related to processes, equipment, facilities and buildings

• Providing scientific input within microbiology, classified areas, cleanrooms, HVAC and validation, and acting as a senior sparring partner who shares knowledge through projects, process groups and specialist networks

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Environmental Monitoring team in M1, part of API Manufacturing in Kalundborg, where we produce active pharmaceutical ingredients for Novo products. In Global Manufacturing & Supply, colleagues work across the value chain to scale processes and products for the people who need them. M1 is an established API production facility, and the EM team supports it in maintaining and developing its controlled and classified production environment.

Your closest partners will be colleagues in production, supporting functions and across Novo. Together, we work in a dynamic production environment where quality, collaboration and continuous improvement are central to our daily work.

Your manager is Berit Eskerod Olsen. As the team is currently short of senior EM capacity, you will have a visible role in supporting colleagues and keeping momentum.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take ownership and make your voice heard, in a team where honest feedback and constructive challenge help everyone raise the bar. You will grow through close collaboration with production and specialist colleagues, building your experience on real EM challenges and sharing your expertise with others.

We support you to perform at your best, with clear expectations and a team that values both quality and pragmatism.

What we offer

As Project Manager in Global Manufacturing & Supply, you will lead medium to high complexity projects from plan to delivery. You will set clear direction, keep scope, quality, schedule and budget on track, and act as a trusted advisor to the line of business (LoB). Your work helps scale the facilities and processes behind treatments for people living with serious chronic diseases, and you will help fellow project managers raise their game.

What you’ll bring

You are an independent Project Manager who combines structure with empathy, and who is at ease in production, building and pharma environments.

• Academic degree (bachelor’s or master’s) in construction, mechanical engineering or similar field

• Solid project management experience (5+ years), including independent delivery of complex projects.

• Experience from production, building and pharma.

• Knowledge of quality assurance and control, and of GMP.

• Understanding of systems and complex projects, and strong planning skills.

• Good knowledge of administrative IT systems, including MS Office and MS Project.

• Fluent English is mandatory, and Danish is considered an advantage

• Empathy for all stakeholders, with a cooperative, team-minded approach.

• A proactive, responsible, flexible and energetic way of working, with a positive attitude and a drive to deliver effectively.

What you’ll do

You will independently run projects of medium to high complexity, as assessed in PEM, and be a role model for project management and project leadership.

• Direct project execution: give the project and its team clear goals and purpose, so time and resources are used well and the team stays motivated.

• Create and develop the project plan: apply the right amount of planning and organising, and set direction for work packages and dependencies.

• Monitor and control the work: keep the end product within scope, quality, schedule and budget, and report project status and accruals to the Steering Group/PPG following standards and governance.

• Manage resources: align project resources with LoB management and steer them during execution.

• Manage risk, stakeholders, change and procurement: maintain the risk map, mitigate or escalate risks and share learnings with other projects. Tailor your approach to each stakeholder, communicate on time, and follow procurement standards with project procurement professionals, locally and corporate.

• Share your knowledge: support and guide other project managers across Novo, coach project teams, and exchange experience with similar projects.

Who you’ll work with

You will be part of DPM HI, PMO, in Global Manufacturing & Supply. In this area, colleagues work across the value chain from drug and device development to marketed Novo products, scaling molecules, processes, devices and products for the people who need them.

Day to day, you will work with your project team, LoB management, the Steering Group/PPG, project procurement professionals and fellow project managers across Novo. You will listen to ideas, challenge solutions within the project scope, and help people align when priorities or interests pull in different directions. Being clear about roles, responsibilities and next steps is how you keep projects moving at pace.

You will be based at 25 A/B in Hillerød. Some travel may be expected.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to run projects independently, with room to make your voice heard and to challenge constructively. You will grow through complex, cross-functional projects, by giving and receiving feedback from fellow project managers, and by coaching others. Clear expectations and a focus on results help you do your best work and be recognised for it.

**_Help customers turn technology into solutions they use every day.

_**At Trackunit, our IrisX industry cloud platform unlocks insights, benchmarks, and innovation through connected construction data. As a Solution Delivery Engineer, you’ll help customers successfully implement and adopt Manager and IrisX, making these platforms part of their everyday operations.

This is a hands-on role at the intersection of engineering, data, and customer engagement. You’ll configure solutions, build integrations, and work with customer teams to translate their needs into practical results. Along the way, you’ll collaborate with colleagues across Trackunit and explore a wide range of technologies and customer environments.

****What’s in it for you

******A broad technical playground

**You’ll work across platform configuration, software development, integrations, and data engineering. Depending on the project, you could use Python and SQL, JavaScript or TypeScript, REST and GraphQL APIs, webhooks and Databricks. There’s room to apply your strengths while building experience in new areas.

**Customer projects with tangible outcomes

**Your work will help construction companies connect their systems, improve their data, and adopt new ways of working. You’ll see solutions through to practical use and understand how your contribution helps customers get more value from Trackunit.

**Collaboration across disciplines

**You’ll work closely with Solution Delivery colleagues, Sales Engineering, IoT Services, Customer Success, Product, and Engineering. You’ll have opportunities to learn from different specialisms, share your knowledge, and contribute customer insights that help improve our platforms.

**Ownership and professional growth

**You’ll take responsibility for meaningful parts of customer delivery, with scope reflecting your experience and strengths. Whether you want to deepen your technical expertise, develop your customer-facing skills, or take on more complex implementations, you’ll have opportunities to grow through practical work, coaching, and feedback.

**The Opportunity To Shape How We Deliver

**Beyond individual projects, you’ll help develop reusable solutions, implementation patterns, and documentation. Your ideas and experience will contribute to making future deliveries more effective across the global Solution Delivery team.

**An international and flexible workplace

**You’ll join a global team that values collaboration, knowledge sharing, and personal development, with a flexible working setup and connections across teams and borders.

****What you’ll work on

******Solution implementation and adoption

**Configure, extend, test, and deploy Manager and IrisX solutions to fit customer workflows and help customers put them into use.

**Integrations and data pipelines

**Connect Trackunit with customer systems such as ERP, CRM, and fleet management tools through APIs, webhooks, and data flows, supporting reliable and secure data exchange.

**Applied data and analytics

**Turn connected construction data into useful insights, supporting use cases such as equipment fault analysis, benchmarking, and emissions reporting, and other customer-specific analytics use cases.

**Customer enablement

**Work with customer teams through technical workshops, training, and implementation support, helping them confidently operate and adopt the solutions delivered.

**Coordinated delivery and continuous improvement

**Collaborate with internal teams and customer stakeholders on implementation activities and clear handovers. Share delivery learnings and customer feedback with Product and Engineering to improve the platform and future deployments.

**Bring your curiosity and perspective

**There are different paths into Solution Delivery. Your experience might come from software engineering, data, integrations, technical consulting, or practical projects that you’re ready to build on.

You don’t need to know every technology we use. We’re interested in how you approach problems, collaborate with others, and connect technical work with customer needs.

If you enjoy building solutions and helping people put them to work, we’d love to hear from you.

**Our hiring process

**We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

**About The Role

**We are looking for an AIT Quality Engineer to join our AIT Project Quality Management team. In this role, you will be responsible for planning, driving, and delivering validation and quality activities within complex Automation and IT projects in the pharmaceutical and life science industry.

You will work as part of multidisciplinary project teams and act as a trusted advisor on validation strategy, GMP compliance, quality risk management, and project quality execution from project initiation through to handover. The role combines hands-on technical validation expertise with project quality management responsibilities, ensuring that deliverables, quality expectations, timelines, and customer requirements are aligned throughout the project lifecycle.

Location Denmark - Kalundborg

Experience Minimum 5 Years

Department AIT Project Quality Management

**As an AIT Quality Engineer, you’ll be:

• Leading CQV and validation activities for automation, IT, computerized systems, and equipment interfaces in GMP-regulated projects.

• Developing and reviewing validation documentation, including URS, FS/DS, SVP, IQ/OQ/PQ, risk assessments, test protocols, and summary reports.

• Executing qualification and testing activities while ensuring compliance with GMP requirements, industry standards, and customer expectations.

• Collaborating with customers, suppliers, and project teams throughout FAT, SAT, commissioning, validation, and handover.

• Managing validation risks, deviations, compliance issues, and mitigation actions across projects.

**Who You Are

**We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you are:

• Able to work independently while building strong relationships with stakeholders.

• Comfortable balancing compliance, quality, timelines, and project risks.

• Eager to share knowledge and support the development of colleagues.

• Skilled at communicating complex validation topics in a practical way.

• Motivated by collaboration and delivering high-quality results in project environments.

• A B.Sc., M.Sc., or equivalent degree in engineering, IT, life sciences, biotechnology, pharmaceutical sciences, or a related field.

• Hands-on experience preparing and reviewing validation documentation, including URS, FS/DS, SVP, IQ/OQ/PQ, risk assessments, and test protocols.

• Knowledge of GMP, GAMP 5, ISPE guidance, data integrity, quality risk management, and validation lifecycle management.

• Ability to advise customers and project teams on validation strategy, compliance risks, and quality-related decisions.

**Life at NNE

You’ll have a say in the first menu, how the kitchen is organised and how the team works together. You’ll work directly with management, with room to put your ideas into practice. Salary will reflect your experience and qualifications.

Interested in leading the kitchen? Apply through this listing with your CV and a few lines about your experience with Italian cooking and kitchen leadership.

Location: Copenhagen office

Hybrid: Three days a week in the office

Language: Fluent English. Norwegian (native or fluent) strongly preferred

Markets: Norway and Sweden

Exciting news: NewGen is expanding into new markets with existing clients. We're building our first in-market team in the Nordics to cover Norway and Sweden. We're looking for local talent to help us launch it and shape how NewGen works in the region from day one.

About NewGen

Welcome to NewGen. We're a global social creative and creator agency made up of over 100 talented people worldwide, with offices in London, Manchester and New York. We partner with leading brands to shape culture, tell stories that matter and harness the power of social first creative and creators to drive meaningful impact. As a fast growing agency with a collaborative, ambitious spirit, we bring together data, strategy, creativity and innovation to deliver work that cuts through, connects and creates conversation.

Founded by our 30-under-30 co-founders, NewGen is an independent agency working with some of the world's biggest brands. Privately owned and built to challenge the big networks and traditional agencies, we move fast, live social and know that fresh ideas can compete with anyone. In fact, we know it's the only way to deliver work consumers care about.

Our work is trusted by some of the world's biggest brands, including Pepsi, Samsung, Amazon, SEGA and CashApp. Just as importantly, we're the agency of choice for leading creators shaping culture today, from KSI and Amelia Dimoldenberg to PewDiePie. When the people driving conversations and influencing audiences trust us, it's no surprise that the world's most ambitious brands do too.

Our Non-Negotiables

• Energy: Get involved, be heard and contribute. This isn't the place for an easy ride. We want people who bring energy and ideas.

• Quality: Quality comes first. If it doesn't feel right, speak up. Everything we create should push boundaries and break new ground.

• Collaboration: We win as a team. No egos, no judgement: just support, collaboration and collective success.

• Creativity: We thrive on fresh thinking. New ideas and bold approaches are what keep us moving forward.

• Partnership: Be a great partner to our clients. Everything we do should deliver on their objectives and create a positive, collaborative experience. This is paramount.

The Role

We're looking for a commercially minded and socially native Account Director to lead our client relationships across Norway and Sweden from Copenhagen. As one of our first in-market hires, you'll own senior day to day client relationships, lead client onboarding and make sure work is strategically sharp, creatively ambitious and commercially strong.

You'll lead the influencer scope from day one, then take on social as it launches. You'll work closely with our in-market influencer managers and social creatives, as well as our strategy, creative and influencer teams in the UK. You are both a leader and a doer. You bring clarity, pace and energy, you know what great looks like and you protect the team while raising standards.

Key Responsibilities

Lead Accounts with Confidence

• Act as senior day to day client lead across Norway and Sweden

• Build trusted relationships with marketing stakeholders in market

• Drive proactive thinking rather than reactive servicing

• Provide clear senior counsel on social strategy and performance

Launch and Onboard

• Lead client onboarding as new scopes start, setting up ways of working, approvals and reporting

• Help build our in-market team and processes from the ground up

• Bring local market knowledge to every brief so the work lands in both markets

Own Delivery Excellence

• Oversee campaign delivery from brief through to wrap

• Make sure timelines, scope and budgets are tightly managed

• Anticipate risk and solve problems early

• Maintain high standards across all outputs

Drive Commercial Performance

• Be accountable for revenue and margin performance

• Identify organic growth opportunities

• Support SOW development and forecasting

• Make sure accounts are properly scoped and resourced

Elevate Strategic Output

• Partner closely with Strategy and Creative so ideas are insight led and socially native

• Make sure deliverables ladder back to client business objectives

• Push for measurable impact across campaigns

Lead and Develop the Team

• Guide and support the in-market team day to day, including influencer managers and social creatives

• Create a high performance, supportive team culture

• Provide clear feedback and development pathways

• Drive accountability and ownership across the team

Champion Collaboration

• Work seamlessly with influencer, creative, production and data teams across markets

• Make sure clients get a joined up experience across disciplines and markets

• Contribute to agency wide initiatives and improvements

Social First x Brand Impact

Being socially native is at the heart of everything we do at NewGen. We're not an advertising agency. We live and breathe culture, constantly plugged into the trends, conversations and creators shaping the world.

To succeed here you need a deep understanding of the creator landscape in Norway and Sweden, an instinct for what resonates online and the ability to turn trends and cultural insight into work that feels authentic, bold and social first. It's ok to be chronically online.

We'd Love You To Have

• Fluent English. Norwegian (native or fluent) strongly preferred

• 8+ years experience in social creative or integrated agency roles

• Experience leading large accounts or multi market campaigns, ideally across the Nordics

• Strong commercial acumen

• Deep knowledge of social platforms and creator culture in the Nordics

• Experience managing and developing teams

• Confident presentation and stakeholder management skills

• Experience working in fast paced agency environments

• Ability to turn creative ideas into measurable business results

About ALK

ALK is a global pharmaceutical company specializing in allergy immunotherapy. We are driven by a high level of professionalism, integrity, an open-minded approach and contributing to an inspiring and fun working environment together with our colleagues. We provide an attractive working environment for individuals looking for both personal and professional development. You will be part of an engaged and informal team who values skill and knowledge creation.

The position

We are looking for a Group Production Controller to support the measurement and follow-up of manufacturing financial performance across ALK Group and its individual production sites.

You will contribute to transparent, consistent, and high-quality financial reporting for the Product Supply leadership team by preparing analyses that improve understanding of COGS and margin development. The role acts as a finance partner to CMC and Group Product Supply support functions, while supporting group budgeting, forecasting, and planning processes for manufacturing costs.

You will work with VPs and other management across ALK Group globally, as well as the Product Supply Finance organization. The role also offers the opportunity to drive transparency, improve financial processes, and simplify and automate reporting and performance management.

This role requires occasional travel, approximately 2–3 times per year.

Responsibilities

• 
Prepare and maintain recurring monthly reporting on manufacturing financial performance.

• 
Monitor results against budgets, forecasts, and targets, explaining variances through operational and financial drivers.

• 
Track operational improvement initiatives and the delivery and financial realization of their benefits.

• 
Act as a day-to-day finance partner to site CMC and Group Product Supply support functions by providing high-quality planning and reporting.

• 
Prepare analyses with clear, actionable insights and recommendations for management and Product Supply stakeholders.

• 
Drive transparency in the cost development of ALK-produced products and the financial performance of Product Supply.

• 
Support the standardization and automation of reporting processes and financial models.

• 
Drive continuous improvement of systems and processes within the area.

Experience and qualifications

• 
Master’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field.

• 
2–4 years of experience in production controlling, FP&A, business finance, or a similar role.

• 
Experience from an industrial or manufacturing environment is preferred.

• 
Experience with performance management, forecasting, budgeting, cost control, and financial performance tracking.

• 
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel.

• 
Familiarity with ERP systems (e.g. SAP) is preferred.

• 
Experience with business intelligence and reporting tools is preferred.

• 
Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to partner effectively across departments.

• 
Proactive and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines.

• 
Fluent written and spoken English.

Become a part of ALK

ALK provides a dynamic and accommodating work environment, complete with inspiring and challenging assignments. You are able to actively influence and challenge the status quo. Our flat structures attract independent individuals who like to feel the progress of the business and enjoy being close to the decision-making process. We consider our pioneering spirit, coupled with our trustworthiness, our winning formula.

Our offices in Denmark offer a green view of the DTU Science Park in Hørsholm. We believe that physical presence enforces strong teamwork and collaboration and creates success, so it is important that you enjoy coming to work at our site with a degree of flexibility to also work from home.

We evaluate applications and call for interviews on an ongoing basis, so don't wait to apply. We reserve the right to take down the advert when we have found the right candidate.

We are looking forward to hearing from you.

About ALK

Allergy impacts and challenges the lives of millions of adults and children every day. At ALK, our purpose is to improve the lives of people living with allergies. Building on our strong heritage, we are guided by our strategy, Allergy+, that shows us a clear path towards this goal through focus, innovation, cultivation and optimisation.

Read more about our corporate strategy and our ambitions for growth

Fair and unbiased recruitment at ALK

At ALK, we believe that every candidate deserves to be evaluated fairly and respectfully. Our recruitment process is designed to give each applicant an equal opportunity, regardless of their background. Read more about fair and unbiased recruitment at ALK.

If you are applying from North America, please know that we are committed to fair, unbiased and non-discriminatory recruitment practices and to complying with all applicable federal, provincial, state, territorial and local employment laws. Employment decisions are made based on qualifications, skills and experience, without discrimination on the basis of legally protected characteristics. jobs.description:
What Makes Us, Us Join some of the most innovative thinkers in FinTech as we lead the evolution of financial technology. If you are an innovative, curious, collaborative person who embraces challenges and wants to grow, learn and pursue outcomes with our prestigious financial clients, say Hello to SimCorp!

At its foundation, SimCorp is guided by our values — caring, customer success-driven, collaborative, curious, and courageous. Our people-centered organization focuses on skills development, relationship building, and client success. We take pride in cultivating an environment where all team members can grow, feel heard, valued, and empowered.

If you like what we’re saying, keep reading!

**WHY THIS ROLE IS IMPORTANT TO US

**We are seeking a highly skilled Lead Software Engineers to drive the design, development, and evolution of our Risk Fusion platform, focused on integrating SimCorp Dimension and Axioma Risk solutions through robust model and position integration capabilities.

**What You Will Be Responsible For

**

• Lead architecture and development of Risk Fusion services.

• Design APIs and ETL pipelines to support seamless integration

• Implement ETL flows to extract instrument T&Cs from SimCorp Dimension, map into Axioma Risk format, and import into Axioma Risk

• Collaborate with Product, Consulting, and QA.

• Develop automated tests for new features.

**What We Value

**

• 7+ years software engineering experience.

• Experience with SQL and REST APIs.

• Experience building ETL pipelines / data integrations.

• Basic understanding of pricing methodologies for financial instruments, including equities, bonds, FX, futures, options, and OTC derivatives.

• Demonstrated problem solving skills.

**Preferred

**

• CFA, FRM or equivalent financial certification

• Understanding of OTC instrument T&Cs (e.g. swaps, FX forwards, TRS).

• Understanding of VaR, Stress Testing, Factor Risk and other Risk Analytics.

• Axioma Risk workflows/integration.

**Benefits

**

• Global hybrid work policy - We ask you to work 2 days a week from the office. If you choose you can work remotely the other days. Of course you are welcome at the office if that is your preference.

• Growth and innovation - Every 6th sprint is reserved for planning and innovation. So, with regular intervals you have a chance to explore and learn new skills or improve something that you believe will be beneficial to you, your team or the application.

• Self-Direction - High degree of self-organization. Each team and developer have a high degree of freedom to plan, organize and design their work.

• Inclusive and diverse company culture

• Work-life balance – We believe that an equilibrium between professional responsibilities makes us all the best version of ourselves, both in private life and as colleagues in the workplace

• Empowerment – We believe that all voices are valuable and must be heard. You will be involved in shaping our work processes

**NEXT STEPS

**Please send us your application in English via our career site as soon as possible, we process incoming applications continually. Please note that only applications sent through our system will be processed. At SimCorp, we recognize that bias can unintentionally occur in the recruitment process. To uphold fairness and equal opportunities for all applicants, we kindly ask you to exclude personal data such as photo, age, or any non-professional information from your application. Thank you for aiding us in our endeavor to mitigate biases in our recruitment process.

If you are interested in being a part of SimCorp but are not sure this role is suitable, submit your CV anyway. SimCorp is on an exciting growth journey, and our Talent Acquisition Team is ready to assist you discover the right role for you. The approximate time to consider your CV is three weeks.

We are eager to continually improve our talent acquisition process and make everyone’s experience positive and valuable. Therefore, during the process we will ask you to provide your feedback, which is highly appreciated.

**Who We Are

**For over 50 years, we have worked closely with investment and asset managers to become the world’s leading provider of integrated investment management solutions. We are 3,000+ colleagues with a broad range of nationalities, educations, professional experiences, ages, and backgrounds.

SimCorp is an independent subsidiary of the Deutsche Börse Group. Following the recent merger with Axioma, we leverage the combined strength of our brands to provide an industry-leading, full, front-to-back offering for our clients.

SimCorp is an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, without regard to race, gender, age, disability, or any other protected status under applicable law. We are committed to building a culture where diverse perspectives and expertise are integrated into our everyday work. We believe in the continual growth and development of our employees, so that we can provide best-in-class solutions to our clients.

Student Assistant- Structural Department

Do you want to kick-start your career in one of Denmark’s largest buildings division? Are you passionate about building technology, structures and structural engineering? And are you curious and ambitious? Then join COWI and develop your potential in a unique professional environment!

JOIN OUR STRUCTURES SECTION IN LYNGBY

At COWI Denmark, you will become part of COWI’s Buildings division. We provide consultancy services for all types of buildings and every aspect of the construction process. We take a holistic approach to projects, focusing on functionality, value, building technology, energy optimization and sustainable solutions.

In this position, you will join our Structures department in Lyngby, which consists of more than 50 structural engineers. You will also be part of a larger multidisciplinary department across the Buildings & Industry division. The team has a strong sense of community and includes both experienced and recently graduated engineers, all of whom contribute professional pride and strong collegial relationships. We have a broad and highly skilled nationwide network that promotes knowledge sharing and professional sparring.

As a student assistant, you will become part of our national team and work closely with the section’s specialists, other student assistants and your immediate manager. Our department delivers a wide range of exciting projects, including Airports, Hospital, Pharma, Water treatment plants, Datacenters, several major and minor renovation projects, and many other interesting assignments. You can look forward to working in a strong professional environment with engaging and developmental tasks, which may include:

• Preparing structural documentation acc. to BR18 and SBi 271.

• Contributing to and supporting professional development and knowledge sharing within the department

• Working with older building cases, including obtaining documentation and reviewing structural documentation

• Assisting the departments specialists on projects by carrying out both administrative and calculation tasks

• Helping facilitate courses and meetings designed to develop the department and keep it up to date with the latest knowledge, technologies, methods and regulations in the construction industry

• Helping to strengthen the social community within the department.

• Support department managers with administrative tasks

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

The first step to success in this role is that you are eager to collaborate with the people around you, whether they are colleagues, partners or customers. Developing ties with others is something you do by acting respectfully and delivering on your promises. And you never get set in your ways, but keep exploring new insights and ways to improve.

On top of that you:

• Are studying engineering within the field of buildings and construction.

• Have knowledge of building technology, structural analysis and structures, including a basic understanding of concrete, steel and timber.

• Have good communication skills in both Danish and English

A place to work and so much more

At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers.

We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home.

With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

Got more questions?

If you have any unanswered questions about the role or what we have to offer, please reach out to Global Talent Acquisition Consultant, Neha Menon at nhme@cowi.com

Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

Before you apply

All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES IN EMPLOYMENT

COWI provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability or genetics. In addition to federal law requirements, COWI complies with applicable state and local laws governing non-discrimination in employment in every location in which the company has facilities. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

Does it excite you to work with late-stage analytical development of innovative peptide-based medicines, and do you have a background in analytical science? If this sounds like you, and you are ready to take on a broad area of responsibilities, then you could be our new colleague.

Your new position

As Analytical Scientist on a 12-month maternity cover, you will support late-stage analytical development across Development and Life Cycle Management (LCM) projects. You will be guided by experienced colleagues and gain hands-on experience in analytical work and in collaboration with Contract Development and Manufacturing Organizations (CDMOs).

We offer exciting responsibilities:

• Support analytical late-stage development activities in Development and LCM projects

• Assist with analytical activities for Drug Substance and Drug Product development, such as stability programs, specifications, extractables and leachable studies, in-use studies, and characterization

• Support the collaboration with CDMOs through day-to-day communication and follow-up on method transfer, validation, and technical and QC activities

• Help prepare scientific reports and documentation that meet requirements for pharmaceutical products

• Assist with scientific input to regulatory documents (NDA/MAA) together with colleagues at Zealand Pharma and CDMOs

• Take part in the Analytical Development team and learn how analytical work contributes to regulatory approval

Your profile

We are looking for someone with an analytical mindset who is curious, careful, and eager to learn. You take ownership of your tasks, ask questions when needed, and enjoy working together with others.

• 
B.Sc., M.Sc., or PhD in chemistry, biochemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, or a related field

• 
Analytical experience from similar role

• 
Familiarity with GMP, late-stage development, or peptide-based products is an advantage, but not a requirement

• 
Interest in working with external partners such as CDMOs, CMOs, and CROs

• 
Good collaboration skills and a structured way of working

• 
Good written and verbal communication skills in English

Your new team

You will join a highly experienced team in Analytical Development, where you will learn from colleagues who share their knowledge. We value a collaborative and supportive atmosphere in which great results are achieved together.

Let's bond and be bold

We have a unique culture, characterized by excellent teamwork and strong engagement across the organization. And we want you to help us strengthen this culture.

Making bonds is at the core of everything we do. From discovering and developing the best new peptide drugs for patients, to engaging with our partners or connecting with each other. We bond through curiosity and playfulness as a team, allowing ourselves to challenge common thinking and drive future innovation. Join us and let's bond and be bold.

Interested in bonding with us? Then please apply no later than November 30, 2026, or as soon as possible. The applications will be reviewed as they come in. While a cover letter is not required, please include a few sentences in your CV explaining your motivation for applying.

For further information, please contact Director, Head of Analytical Development, Iben Almar Meier; imeier@zealandpharma.com.

We are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and welcome applications from all job applicants.

About Zealand Pharma A/S

Zealand Pharma A/S (Nasdaq: ZEAL) is a biotechnology company focused on advancing medicines for obesity and metabolic health. Combining more than 25 years of peptide R&D expertise with a proprietary data platform that leverages advanced data-driven and AI/ML approaches, Zealand Pharma aims to lead a new era in obesity and metabolic health. To date, more than ten Zealand Pharma-invented drug candidates have entered clinical development, of which two products have reached the market and three candidates are in late-stage development. The Company has collaborations with global pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners for research, development, and commercialization. Founded in 1998, Zealand Pharma is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, with a U.S. presence in Boston, Massachusetts. Learn more at www.zealandpharma.com.
